title: L2b — pair contrast: does recording the failure add anything?
notes: Two protocols, one corpus, one teaching schedule: 6 questions in round one, 2 revisions in round two, 8 evaluated, 1 of them unreachable by construction.
single: one attempt, completed, then corrected. pair: attempt one completed and recorded as a failure (wrong-mark), attempt two from the same pack completed and corrected, linked by parentRunId.
Attempt two does not re-recall: the store is not distilled between attempts, so a second read returns the same pack. The variable under test is the recorded failure, not retrieval noise.

The revision round is what makes the comparison non-vacuous: 2 questions are re-asked after their convention moved, so the corrected attempt retrieves a rule that is now wrong. Both arms corrected all 2; the lever fired.
Cross-arm store diff: 0 rule(s) differ. An empty diff with a zero delta says the recorded failure changed nothing measurable — not that the experiment failed to look.

Reachable share 75.00%: the questions whose (domain, intent) key was taught. The remainder is the held-out convention, which no correction could supply — a fixed cost the recovery denominator does not hide.

Recovery is (arm - baseline) / (oracle - baseline) on the whole holdout, with oracle 1.00 by construction: the gold is the stated convention. The bar for calling a difference an improvement is 0.05 of recovery.
Verdict: pair helps = false; delta 0.00pp against a 5pp bar. A null result is a result — the failure record is not called an improvement because it was tried.
Corrected attempts that cited a rule: 2/7 single, 2/7 pair. The lever was exercised, so the delta is a measurement of the recorded failure rather than of an empty store.
The artefact carries 6/6 gates: headroom, a real wall, a split with both mass and a wall, and evidence that the failure was actually recorded.
